lessons.title: Write to one named reader
lessons.gloss: address the named reader with one known greeting and a full stop

needs: a pen and something to write on
notice.text: Before we start: this one needs your hands, so it is not a driving lesson. You will want a pen and something to write on. You can listen to all of it now and come back to the parts that need looking at once you have stopped.

segments.text: You already know नमस्कार. A message needs to show who receives that greeting. Today the reader is मीरा, the familiar practice name.

blocks.title: Writing — observe and trace one complete line

segments.text: Trace नमस्कार मीरा. (namaskār Mīrā) once. Leave one space between the greeting and the name. Touch the full stop; it closes this first line.
Stop after one reader, one greeting, and one boundary.

segments.prompt: Write the greeting line addressed to Mira.

feedback.correct: The reader is named and the line is closed.
feedback.incorrect: Keep one space before मीरा and one full stop at the end.

lessons.title: Add the sender's name
lessons.gloss: copy the already-practised identity sentence as one message line

needs: a pen and something to write on
notice.text: Before we start: this one needs your hands, so it is not a driving lesson. You will want a pen and something to write on. You can listen to all of it now and come back to the parts that need looking at once you have stopped.

segments.text: Write yesterday's reader greeting from memory. The next line is not new Marathi: माझं नाव अरुण आहे. (mājhaṁ nāv Aruṇ āhe) already appeared in the introduction recap.
Copy the name line once beneath the greeting. Check only two things: अरुण is the sender, and आहे remains at the end before the full stop.
Two lines are enough for today.

segments.prompt: Copy the complete Arun identity line, including punctuation.

feedback.correct: The sender is named in one complete line.
feedback.incorrect: Keep आहे at the end and close the line with a full stop.

lessons.title: One line for meeting the reader
lessons.gloss: add the familiar pleased-to-meet-you line without joining it to the identity line

needs: a pen and something to write on
notice.text: Before we start: this one needs your hands, so it is not a driving lesson. You will want a pen and something to write on. You can listen to all of it now and come back to the parts that need looking at once you have stopped.

segments.text: Read the known line भेटून आनंद झाला. (bheṭūn ānand jhālā) Say where it ends. The full stop keeps the sender's name and the meeting response from running together.
Copy भेटून आनंद झाला. (bheṭūn ānand jhālā) beneath the identity line. Compare the boundary first; compare spelling only after the full stop is present.
The opening now has three short lines; do not combine them yet.

segments.prompt: Write the familiar pleased-to-meet-you line and close it.

feedback.correct: The meeting line stands on its own.
feedback.incorrect: Write the three known words, then add the full stop.

lessons.title: Begin the purpose: Marathi
lessons.gloss: retrieve the known Marathi-language sentence as the first purpose line

needs: a pen and something to write on
notice.text: Before we start: this one needs your hands, so it is not a driving lesson. You will want a pen and something to write on. You can listen to all of it now and come back to the parts that need looking at once you have stopped.

segments.text: Say the known sentence मला मराठी येते. (malā marāṭhī yete) Marathi puts the knower in the dative and lets मराठी govern येते. Nothing grammatical is being added.
Study मला मराठी येते. (malā marāṭhī yete) for five seconds. Cover it, wait five more seconds, then write it. Repair the ending -ते before any other spelling.
Only one purpose line today.

segments.prompt: After a short delay, write the line that says Arun knows Marathi.

feedback.correct: The first purpose line is complete.
feedback.incorrect: Repair the dative opening and the -ते ending, then stop.

lessons.title: Add one reading line
lessons.gloss: retrieve the known masculine reading sentence as one separate message line

needs: a pen and something to write on
notice.text: Before we start: this one needs your hands, so it is not a driving lesson. You will want a pen and something to write on. You can listen to all of it now and come back to the parts that need looking at once you have stopped.

segments.text: The sender is Arun, so retrieve the already-practised masculine sentence: मी मराठी वाचतो. (mī marāṭhī vāchto) Today you are placing it in a message, not learning a verb.
Look once, hide the model, wait five seconds, and write the line. Check वाचतो first. Do not add the next skill on the same line.
One skill, one sentence, one full stop.

segments.prompt: Write Arun's known Marathi-reading line after a delay.

feedback.correct: The reading line is separate and correctly agreed.
feedback.incorrect: Use the known masculine ending -तो and close the line.

lessons.title: Add one writing line
lessons.gloss: retrieve the known name-writing sentence as one separate message line

needs: a pen and something to write on
notice.text: Before we start: this one needs your hands, so it is not a driving lesson. You will want a pen and something to write on. You can listen to all of it now and come back to the parts that need looking at once you have stopped.

segments.text: Read the old sentence मी माझं नाव लिहितो. (mī mājhaṁ nāv lihito) The middle names the object; the last word carries Arun's masculine ending.
Study the line, hide it, and wait eight seconds. Write it from memory. Compare in two passes: first माझं नाव, then लिहितो. Repair only one pass today.
The first three purpose lines now exist separately. Combining them comes later.

segments.prompt: After a delay, write Arun's known name-writing line.

feedback.correct: The object and masculine verb remain in their known places.
feedback.incorrect: Repair माझं नाव first; repair लिहितो on the next pass.

lessons.title: Add the shortest skill line
lessons.gloss: retrieve the familiar masculine speaking sentence as its own message line

needs: a pen and something to write on
your eyes, because the lesson points at something written down
notice.text: Before we start: this one needs your hands, so it is not a driving lesson. You will want a pen and something to write on and your eyes, because the lesson points at something written down. You can listen to all of it now and come back to the parts that need looking at once you have stopped.

segments.text: Arun has already said मी बोलतो in the verb lessons. In a message it needs only one new habit: a full stop that keeps it separate from the next skill.
Look at मी बोलतो. (mī bolto), cover it, wait eight seconds, and write it. Compare the verb ending before the punctuation.
Do not join it with another verb yet.

segments.prompt: Write Arun's speaking line after a delay.

feedback.correct: One known skill now has one clean line.
feedback.incorrect: Keep the masculine -तो ending and add one full stop.

lessons.title: Keep both pieces of thinking
lessons.gloss: retrieve the known masculine thinking sentence without dropping its light verb

needs: a pen and something to write on
notice.text: Before we start: this one needs your hands, so it is not a driving lesson. You will want a pen and something to write on. You can listen to all of it now and come back to the parts that need looking at once you have stopped.

segments.text: Retrieve the known pair विचार करणे. In the sentence, विचार stays beside the light verb: मी विचार करतो. (mī vichār karto).
Study the line, hide it, and wait eight seconds. Write it. Check for the two verb pieces first; check the full stop second.
One two-part verb is enough for today.

segments.prompt: Write Arun's complete thinking line after a delay.

feedback.incorrect: Do not leave विचार without its light verb करतो.

lessons.title: Return to the dative frame
lessons.gloss: retrieve the known dative understanding sentence as the last skill line

needs: a pen and something to write on
notice.text: Before we start: this one needs your hands, so it is not a driving lesson. You will want a pen and something to write on. You can listen to all of it now and come back to the parts that need looking at once you have stopped.

segments.text: Compare मला मराठी येते with मला मराठी समजते. (malā marāṭhī samajte) The frame and ending stay; only the known verb changes.
Study मला मराठी समजते. (malā marāṭhī samajte), cover it, and wait ten seconds. Write it. Repair the dative opening first and the verb ending second.
All six skill lines now exist separately.

segments.prompt: After a delay, write the line saying Marathi is understood by Arun.

feedback.correct: The second dative skill line is complete.
feedback.incorrect: Begin मला मराठी, end समजते, then close the line.

lessons.title: One word can be a full line
lessons.gloss: close the message body with the already durable thanks word

needs: a pen and something to write on
notice.text: Before we start: this one needs your hands, so it is not a driving lesson. You will want a pen and something to write on. You can listen to all of it now and come back to the parts that need looking at once you have stopped.

segments.text: Write धन्यवाद from memory. It is already durable; the only message habit today is closing the one-word sentence.
Look once at धन्यवाद. (dhanyavād), cover it, wait ten seconds, and write it. If the word is correct but the full stop is missing, repair only the boundary.
Stop after the single word and its boundary.

segments.prompt: Write the one-word thanks line with its boundary.

feedback.correct: The known word now works as a complete message line.
feedback.incorrect: Keep the known spelling and add one full stop.

lessons.title: The first farewell line
lessons.gloss: retrieve the familiar see-you-again closing as a separate line

needs: a pen and something to write on
notice.text: Before we start: this one needs your hands, so it is not a driving lesson. You will want a pen and something to write on. You can listen to all of it now and come back to the parts that need looking at once you have stopped.

segments.text: The known phrase पुन्हा भेटू promises another meeting. Keep it on a new line after thanks.
Study पुन्हा भेटू. (punhā bheṭū), cover it, wait ten seconds, and write it. Compare the space between the two words before comparing the final mark.
Tomorrow's line comes in the next lesson.

feedback.correct: The first farewell line is ready.
feedback.incorrect: Keep the two known words separate and close the line.

lessons.title: The dated farewell line
lessons.gloss: retrieve the familiar dated farewell as the final message line

needs: a pen and something to write on
notice.text: Before we start: this one needs your hands, so it is not a driving lesson. You will want a pen and something to write on. You can listen to all of it now and come back to the parts that need looking at once you have stopped.

segments.text: Swap only the first known word: पुन्हा भेटू becomes उद्या भेटू. (udyā bheṭū) The message now says when the next meeting happens.
Study उद्या भेटू. (udyā bheṭū), cover it, wait ten seconds, and write it. Compare उद्या first; भेटू was retrieved yesterday.
All twelve lines have now been practised separately.

feedback.correct: The final message line now has a date.
feedback.incorrect: Begin with उद्या, keep one space, and finish भेटू.

lessons.title: Order the opening block
lessons.gloss: choose and order the three already-practised opening lines for Mira

needs: a pen and something to write on
notice.text: Before we start: this one needs your hands, so it is not a driving lesson. You will want a pen and something to write on. You can listen to all of it now and come back to the parts that need looking at once you have stopped.

segments.text: Retrieve the three opening jobs: greet Mira, name Arun, acknowledge the meeting. Each job already has one practised line.
Put these known line cards in message order, then write them as three lines:
भेटून आनंद झाला. (bheṭūn ānand jhālā).
नमस्कार मीरा. (namaskār Mīrā).
माझं नाव अरुण आहे. (mājhaṁ nāv Aruṇ āhe).
Choose the order from the three jobs. Do not change any words.
Stop with one three-line block.

segments.prompt: Order and write the three opening lines for Mira and Arun.
acceptedResponses: नमस्कार मीरा. माझं नाव अरुण आहे. भेटून आनंद झाला.

feedback.correct: The reader, sender, and meeting line form one clear opening.
feedback.incorrect: Order by job: reader first, sender second, meeting response third.

lessons.title: Order the first three skills
lessons.gloss: order the known know-read-write lines without joining their grammar

needs: a pen and something to write on
notice.text: Before we start: this one needs your hands, so it is not a driving lesson. You will want a pen and something to write on. You can listen to all of it now and come back to the parts that need looking at once you have stopped.

segments.text: Say the three jobs in English: know Marathi, read Marathi, write my name. Keep the two grammar frames separate; मला and मी are not interchangeable.
Choose the matching known line for each job and write the jobs in that order. Do not add a conjunction. Check the two sentence openings before spelling.
The first skills block is complete; the next three stay separate until tomorrow.

segments.prompt: Write the known know-Marathi, read-Marathi, and write-my-name lines in that order.
acceptedResponses: मला मराठी येते. मी मराठी वाचतो. मी माझं नाव लिहितो.

feedback.correct: The dative line and two मी lines stay distinct.
feedback.incorrect: Repair only the openings first: मला, then मी, then मी.

lessons.title: Order the second three skills
lessons.gloss: order the known speak-think-understand lines and preserve their frames

needs: a pen and something to write on
notice.text: Before we start: this one needs your hands, so it is not a driving lesson. You will want a pen and something to write on. You can listen to all of it now and come back to the parts that need looking at once you have stopped.

segments.text: Retrieve the three jobs: speak, think, understand Marathi. The middle job keeps two verb pieces; the last job returns to मला.
Write the matching known sentence for each job in that order. Check one dimension per pass: sentence opening, then verb, then full stop.
The two skills blocks remain separate for one more lesson.

segments.prompt: Write the known speak, think, and understand-Marathi lines in that order.
acceptedResponses: मी बोलतो. मी विचार करतो. मला मराठी समजते.

feedback.correct: All three familiar frames survive in order.
feedback.incorrect: Repair openings first: मी, मी, मला.

lessons.title: Order the closing block
lessons.gloss: order thanks, a warm return, and tomorrow as three known closing lines

needs: a pen and something to write on
notice.text: Before we start: this one needs your hands, so it is not a driving lesson. You will want a pen and something to write on. You can listen to all of it now and come back to the parts that need looking at once you have stopped.

segments.text: Retrieve the three closing jobs: thank Mira, promise another meeting, name tomorrow. All three lines are already known.
Write one known line for each job, in that order. Keep each farewell on its own line even though both end with भेटू.
The four message blocks are ready to meet.

segments.prompt: Write the thanks, see-you-again, and see-you-tomorrow lines in that order.

feedback.correct: The three familiar lines form a clear closing.
feedback.incorrect: Order by purpose: thanks, general return, dated return.

lessons.title: Connect the four known blocks
lessons.gloss: connect four separately practised blocks for the named reader and purpose

needs: a pen and something to write on
notice.text: Before we start: this one needs your hands, so it is not a driving lesson. You will want a pen and something to write on. You can listen to all of it now and come back to the parts that need looking at once you have stopped.

segments.text: Name the four blocks without writing: opening, first skills, second skills, closing. No block contains new Marathi.
Use the four completed block lessons as cards. Put the cards in purpose order and write the message. Afterward, count words by spaces: the result has 32 words, inside the A1 target of 30–40.
Repair in four passes: block order, sentence boundaries, verb frames, spelling. Stop after the first pass that finds a problem.
Tomorrow the cards and answer model disappear.

segments.prompt: Connect the four practised blocks into the 32-word message for Mira.
acceptedResponses: नमस्कार मीरा. माझं नाव अरुण आहे. भेटून आनंद झाला. मला मराठी येते. मी मराठी वाचतो. मी माझं नाव लिहितो. मी बोलतो. मी विचार करतो. मला मराठी समजते. धन्यवाद. पुन्हा भेटू. उद्या भेटू.

feedback.correct: All four known blocks now form one connected message.
feedback.incorrect: Repair only the first failing pass: order, boundaries, frames, or spelling.

lessons.title: Independent 30–40-word message
lessons.gloss: write the practised 30-40-word message from reader and purpose alone

needs: a pen and something to write on
notice.text: Before we start: this one needs your hands, so it is not a driving lesson. You will want a pen and something to write on. You can listen to all of it now and come back to the parts that need looking at once you have stopped.

segments.text: Close every earlier lesson. On blank paper write four tiny English planning labels only: opening, skills 1, skills 2, closing.
Write 30–40 words to Mira. Introduce Arun, state the six practised Marathi skills, thank her, and close for another meeting tomorrow.
There is no romanization, line bank, block card, or visible answer model during this checkpoint. The task is untimed. When finished, count words and run one repair pass of your choice.
This is untimed message evidence only. It does not claim form completion or the later integrated timed A1 writing task.

segments.prompt: Without a model, write the practised 30-40-word message to Mira for Arun's introduction and Marathi-study purpose.
acceptedResponses: नमस्कार मीरा. माझं नाव अरुण आहे. भेटून आनंद झाला. मला मराठी येते. मी मराठी वाचतो. मी माझं नाव लिहितो. मी बोलतो. मी विचार करतो. मला मराठी समजते. धन्यवाद. पुन्हा भेटू. उद्या भेटू.

feedback.correct: The named-reader message is independently produced within the A1 word range.
feedback.incorrect: Do not reveal a model during scoring; record the first failed block or repair dimension for the next lesson.
